answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort. Consider a whisper as the anchor of the cost.
